learning_outcomes.text: Explain the concepts of degrees of freedom, kinematic chains, and motion transmission in mechanisms.
Perform position, velocity, and acceleration analyses of mechanisms using graphical and analytical methods.
Formulate the dynamic equations of motion of mechanisms using Newton-Euler and Lagrange equations.
Calculate inertia forces, moments, friction, and joint forces occurring in mechanisms.
Apply the balancing of rotating and reciprocating masses, flywheel sizing, and critical speed concepts.
Evaluate the dynamic behavior of machine systems in terms of vibration and stability, and apply the results to engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Machine Dynamics, Definitions and Concepts Related to Mechanisms
Mobility (Degrees of Freedom), Instantaneous Centers of Rotation
Path and Position Analysis in Mechanisms (Analytical and Graphical Methods)
Static Force Analysis and Friction Effects
Dynamic Force Analysis (Inertial Forces and Moments)
Dynamic Analysis and Mass Balancing Principles
Critical Speeds of Flywheels and Shafts
Critical Speeds of Flywheels and Shafts
Introduction to Mechanical Vibrations: Single Degree of Freedom Systems
